I recently discovered Sketchfab while working on my portfolio website, and honestly, I didn't expect to find something this cool.

I was looking for 3D models to use on my Minecraft-themed portfolio and came across Sketchfab.

And then I went down a rabbit hole. 😂

There are so many 3D models on there, from characters and environments to completely random things I never would have thought someone had already created in 3D.

What surprised me even more was how easy it is to actually view and interact with the models directly in the browser.

I ended up spending way more time exploring models than I probably should have.

It also made me realize how much work goes into creating the 3D assets that we usually just see as part of a website or game.

Definitely one of those things I wish I'd discovered earlier.

#Sketchfab #3DDesign #WebDevelopment #WebDesign #Minecraft #Portfolio #Learning

My obsession with custom loyalty features almost broke our checkout flow.

We were trying to build a unique rewards layer on top of MedusaJS to keep our customers coming back. The logic seemed sound on paper, but integrating it into the core checkout meant overriding default behaviors that were never meant to be touched.

I eventually had to strip back the custom logic and rebuild it as a modular plugin to keep the core codebase stable. Customizing an open-source framework is great until you realize you are fighting against the architecture instead of working with it.

How do you balance adding unique features against maintaining the integrity of your base framework?

#MedusaJS #WebDevelopment #SoftwareEngineering

The Razorpay webhook integration is a minefield of edge cases.

Last month, we had a series of payment notifications that simply refused to sync correctly. It turned out that the webhook events were firing in an order I had not anticipated, which left our backend state in total disarray.

I ended up rewriting the entire listener to handle out-of-order events instead of expecting a clean sequence. Learning how to build defensively for third-party API behavior is a skill they do not really teach in tutorials.

What was the last API integration that gave you a massive headache?

#Razorpay #Backend #WebDevelopment #Coding

When we were setting up the early versions of STRAYED, I wanted to include every feature that crossed my mind. That was until I saw how much bloat it added to our development cycle and our final page load speeds.

I learned to cut features that did not directly improve the checkout flow. Focusing on a smaller set of features meant we could actually refine them until they worked perfectly instead of having a site full of broken promises.

Debugging is mostly about learning to trust your own logs.

There was a time when I spent an entire afternoon looking for a logical error in our database queries while the fix was hidden in plain sight in the console logs. I was looking for complexity where there was only a simple mapping mistake.

Sometimes the best way to solve a bug is to step away from the keyboard and rethink the assumption you made at the start. The code rarely lies, but your perspective on it might be skewed.

Customer feedback is the only real metrics report that matters.

When we started seeing issues with our checkout flow on specific devices, I did not find the answer in a dashboard. I found it by listening to what our users were actually telling us in their emails and support requests.

Numbers tell you that something is wrong, but users tell you exactly where they are getting stuck. Always prioritize the feedback loop that comes directly from the people using your product.

Manual data entry for product variants in Odoo is a massive time sink. 

When we were scaling the catalog for Prettiva and Co, I found myself clicking through the interface to create variations for each item. It was repetitive and error-prone, turning what should be a ten-minute task into an hour of administrative frustration. 

I eventually stopped fighting the manual UI and shifted everything to Excel imports. It allowed me to map out all the variants and attributes in a structured grid before pushing them into the system in one go. Sometimes the most advanced software feature you can use is the one that lets you bypass the interface entirely. 

What is the most tedious workflow you have ever automated to save your sanity? 

#Odoo #Ecommerce #Automation #Startup
